English.Char_Desc_45: Piano for mere mortals - play pop on a synth
English.Char_Desc_80: Play and practice pop songs on piano and drums in a fancy pianoroll on linux
English.Char_Desc_250: Play and practice a pop song on piano and drums in a fancy pianoroll. You practice the piano parts and the background tracks sync to your tempo. Notes are simplified to one per hand max, on 10 keys. Free and open source.
English.Char_Desc_450: Play and practice a pop song on piano and drums in a "pianoroll" format that's kinda fancy. You practice the piano parts and the background tracks sync to your tempo. The aim is to get a simplified song into your head and fingers: the real notes are simplified down to one note per hand max, and your hands stay in one position. Tracks in any midi file can become a song to practice. Free, MIT licensed, on Flathub.
English.Char_Desc_2000:
We have computers. We don't need 88 keys anymore! PianoCheetah lets you play a song with your feel on 10 keys max.
Play and practice a pop song on piano and drums in a "pianoroll" format that's kinda fancy. You practice the piano parts and the background tracks sync to your tempo.
The aim is to get a simplified song into your head and fingers. The real notes of the song are simplified down to one note per hand max, and your hands stay in one position.
Tracks in any midi file can become a song for you to practice and play. Works with midi keyboards and drum pads, and has a built in software synth (syn) if you don't have a sound module.
PianoCheetah was formerly known as PianoCheater. It is free and open source (MIT license) and installs from Flathub - just search for pianocheetah in KDE Discover or Gnome Software.
